correctness.rationale: Stationary affine recurrence gives an independent Laplace current-cycle innovation. The strict contraction bound and bounded shifts provide an exponential moment of the past-cycle remainder at parameter strictly larger than the Laplace rate, making the stationary upper tail asymptotically one Laplace tail. The conditional excess tends to Exp(lambda). On fixed horizons a first Poisson reset necessarily falls below an extreme threshold with probability tending to one, so the residual exit time is asymptotically the minimum of an independent Exp(r) alarm and the standard Brownian first hit from the Exp(lambda) excess. Reflection and an explicit erfc mixture give the Gamma-half survival, with parameters lambda=sqrt(2r)/sigma. A complete reset gives exact finite-threshold equality. Deterministic exact-rational and quadrature checks supplement, not replace, this infinite proof. The statement does not infer mean convergence from weak convergence.

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is a high-stationary-exceedance *forward exit clock* joint law with Gamma-half marginal under bounded random affine contractions. It is not the previously established stationary fixed-point equation, the stationary exponential spatial tail, a long-time Yaglom conditional law, or a conditional reset-age law. Inspected close published results do not state or imply the joint high-level exit-time limit without the new rare-overshoot/first-reset coupling and mixture calculation. Historical coverage by an unindexed general rare-event theorem is a residual risk, not evidence of coverage. Singh–Pal (2022) contains the fixed-start fixed-reset first-passage kernel underpinning the complete-reset benchmark; the new claim is the rare-height stationary coupling for arbitrary uniformly contractive random affine marks.
residual_risks: Rare-exceedance cluster and extreme-event temporal laws could be consequences of a general theorem not located by current semantic and textual searches.
A publication-priority search cannot certify global novelty; independent domain-specialist review remains needed.

value.rationale: Conditioning on a large stationary observation naturally asks how long that unusually elevated excursion lasts; spatial tail formulas do not answer this dynamical residual-lifetime question. The result determines the full coupled overshoot/exit law over an entire robust class of signed random affine reset maps, and discovers a parameter-free Gamma shape and exact complete-reset benchmark. It clarifies that far-tail height selection does not lengthen the future excursion to order of the observed height, because the first reset kills it. It is substantially more than a numerical constant or a routine change of notation; it provides a stable extreme-event duration calibration and separates one-time stationary tails from future persistence.
